findings.code_snippet:
ts workspace ID from that environment variable. Pass `--host <id>` consistently for a remote host. If the target host is offline, use `hosts wake <id>` and confirm it is online before dispatching. To run workers on a machine that is not a host yet but that the user can SSH into, `superset hosts add <ssh-target>` installs the CLI there, signs it in, and keeps it running as a user service. It changes that machine, so get the user's go-ahead first and pass `--yes` only after they agree. It needs `ssh <ssh-target>` to already work from here, and on the remote: macOS or glibc Linux (x64 or arm64, not Alpine or Windows), `curl`, and on Linux a valid `/etc/machine-id` and systemd user services. Without `gh` signed in there, private repos will not clone on that host. Running it again on the same target repairs a broken setup, and `superset hosts remove <ssh-target>` undoes it. Do not use `--agent superset`: it creates a chat session, and terminal read/send cannot control it.
